title: Enterprise outbound hypothesis lab
content:
Context and goal:
- Quick scratchpad for outreach to BlueAtlas Logistics (horizontal logistics / TMS provider). Target: secure a short pilot (3 months) to validate LLM-assisted freight EDI reconciliation and conversational dispatch support.
- Hypothesis: BlueAtlas needs lower-latency, cheaper on-demand reasoning + structured outputs (JSON tool-calls) vs their current vendor who has high cost per token and intermittent latency spikes. Redwood's Dedicated or Private offering could be a strong fit.

Account snapshot (public signals quick scan):
- HQ: Austin, TX; 400–600 employees; Series C in 2024; growing North American carrier integrations.
- Recent hires: Head of Platform (ex-TMS startup), several infra engineers listed on LinkedIn (likely owns model integrations).
- Product: TMS + a web UI for brokers; they launched an internal "exception processing" dashboard in 2025.
- Tech: Postgres + Kafka + AWS (us-east primary). No explicit ML team listed; might be using vendors for NLU.

Initial value props to test (ranked):
1) Error reconciliation templates + deterministic structured outputs (reduce manual exceptions by 30–50%).
2) Low-latency chat assistant embedded in dispatcher UI (95th pct latency SLA, <150ms generate token where possible).
3) Batch embeddings + reranking for document matching (manifest / BOL) to reduce search time / improve match accuracy.

Stakeholder map / personas (to validate):
- Primary champion: Director of Platform (likely cares about latency, infra costs, deployment model).
- Economic buyer: VP of Ops / Head of Product (wants reduction in manual headcount on exceptions).
- Technical blocker: Lead infra/ops engineer (concerns: data residency, throughput, integration complexity).

Key hypotheses to probe on first call:
- H1: Current vendor cost per month is high because they pay for long context windows and do synchronous large-batch processing.
- H2: They have 1–2 high-throughput routes (EDI reconciliation + chat) that would benefit from dedicated GPU capacity.
- H3: Security/compliance is top-of-mind; private VPC or on-prem option will move the needle.

Metrics to quantify if pilot accepted:
- Reduction in FTE hours per week on exceptions (target: 25% after month 1, 50% by month 3).
- Avg time to resolution for exception tickets down from baseline X minutes to Y.
- Per-request cost delta vs current vendor (show forecasted cost/save).

Notes / quick rebuttals (objection handling)
- "We're already using Vendor X": ask for current SLA + cost per reconciliation. Offer a small single-route side-by-side benchmark (no-risk) — Redwood will run 3k requests and show latency/cost tradeoffs.
- "We can't send data to external API": propose Redwood Private (VPC) or dedicated offering; note we can do a self-hosted on-prem proof-of-concept for PII-heavy flows.
- "We worry about hallucinations": emphasize structured output + function/tool calls and regressions/evals tied to prompt sets. Offer to run a 2-week eval on historical exceptions and surface precision/recall.
- "Integration overhead": highlight SDKs + example webhook connector for their Kafka streams and lightweight edge library for in-UI streaming.

Cold outbound sequence (first-pass drafts):
1) Short intro email (subject: "Pilot idea: cut BlueAtlas exception load by 30%"):
Hey [Name],
I saw BlueAtlas recently launched an exception dashboard — congrats. I work on pilot programs at Redwood Inference (inference platform for teams running LLMs in production).
Would you be open to a short 20-minute call to explore a no-risk side-by-side benchmark that compares your current reconciliation flow with a dedicated route we can spin up and run on historical data? We usually surface latency, per-request cost, and hit/miss rates in under a week.
2) LinkedIn note (connect then message):
Connect: "Following BlueAtlas' exception dashboard — would love to connect and share a short pilot idea."
Follow-up message after connect: "Quick note — we've run similar pilots for two TMS vendors and found 20–40% fewer manual exceptions when we pair structured outputs with prefix caching. Can I share a one-pager?"
3) If no response -> short value-add email with example metric: "Pilot template: 3k historical exceptions -> show 95th latency, per-request cost, FTE estimate"

Call outline (20–25m):
- 0:00–2:00 intro + objective (mutual discovery)
- 2:00–8:00 current flow + pain points (who touches exceptions? SLA?)
- 8:00–12:00 proposed pilot (scope: one route — EDI reconciliation or dispatcher chat)
- 12:00–18:00 technical constraints (data residency, throughput needs, auth)
- 18:00–22:00 commercial framing and next steps (pilot timeline, success metrics, cost model)
- 22:00–25:00 close: ask for dataset / sample requests + champion alignment

Data ask for pilot (minimal):
- 2–4 weeks historical exceptions (anonymized) or exported EDI messages (CSV/NDJSON).
- A sample of typical latency/SLA requirements and peak qps windows.
- Contact for infra onboarding (SRE/Platform).

Open questions / TODOs
- Validate whether BlueAtlas uses SSO that would complicate access to logs (ask in discovery).
- Get estimate of monthly exception volume (tickets/month) — crucial for pricing model.
- Draft short SOW template for a 3-month pilot with clear success gates. Omar to propose starter SOW template.

Quick pricing sketch to prepare for call:
- Option A: Hosted pilot (low friction) — fixed flat fee + per-token for evaluation; highlight fast setup but limited data residency guarantees.
- Option B: Dedicated reserved route (recommended if 20k+ reqs/day) — monthly commitment, predictable unit economics, SLA.
- Option C: Private (VPC) — higher setup + infra fee, recommended for customers with strict compliance.

Personal notes to self (tone + pull-through):
- Keep first email short and metrics-forward. Mention a comparable client (anonymized) if asked.
- If they push security, surface Private + a short diagram of control plane vs data plane.
- Bring product engineer to the discovery call if they ask low-level kernel/quantization questions.

Next steps (this doc):
- [ ] Reach out to Director of Platform (LinkedIn + email) next Tue (Mar 17).
- [ ] Omar: prep SOW skeleton + sample metric dashboard (due Mar 19).
- [ ] Leah: pull anonymized exception volume benchmarking template (due Mar 18).
- [ ] Draft follow-up one-pager to attach after first call (Maya).

Scratch/brain dump (fragments):
- Could pitch caching/KV reuse as immediate win for recurring EDI patterns.
- Consider short-term UX: streaming suggestions in dispatcher UI to cut round trips.
- Potential KPIs revenue tied: reduction of detention/late-fee exposure by faster matching -> interesting angle for Econ buyer.

Unresolved / risks:
- They may have internal roadmap to build LLM features in-house; need to surface timeline.
- Unknown license constraints with carriers / third parties for sending manifests to 3P.

(End of scratchpad)
